10 best gifts for student pilots, from first lesson to first solo

The best gift for a student pilot fits the stage they are at. Someone booking a first lesson needs different things from someone preparing for a checkride. Start with one question: what has their instructor actually recommended?

By Pilot Gift Guide · How we choose

IN THIS GUIDEStart with the instructor’s listFor the first few lessonsFor someone already trainingMake a milestone gift personalWhat should you avoid?The listRelated guides

Start with the instructor’s list

Before buying training equipment, find out what the school already supplies and what the instructor expects the student to bring. A duplicate logbook or an incompatible tablet holder is less helpful than a simple gift card. You do not need to understand every piece of equipment: ask the student for a photo or link to their list. If you want to keep the surprise, ask which category is still missing without choosing a model yet.

For the first few lessons

A modest, practical gift is often enough. A logbook can mark the beginning of training if the school has not already supplied one. A pen is easy to add, and a compact light may be useful as the student builds a flight bag. Keep a gift receipt. Avoid buying a complete bundle simply because it says student pilot; the school may have a different syllabus, preferred materials or equipment requirements.

For someone already training

Pay attention to what they carry. A compact flight bag can help if everything currently goes into a general backpack. A kneeboard makes sense only if it fits their exact tablet and they prefer that setup in the cockpit. Ask about the tablet case as well as the iPad model. A headset is a bigger decision: make it a choose-together gift with the student and instructor instead of guessing at connectors or fit.

Make a milestone gift personal

For a first solo or certificate, the story can matter more than the price. A model of the aircraft they actually flew is a better match than a more expensive model of an unrelated airplane. Confirm the type and variant before buying. Add a handwritten note with the date and the moment you are celebrating. For a flight lesson contribution, arrange payment directly with the school and confirm how credit is applied and whether it expires.

What should you avoid?

Do not assume that a flight simulator accessory, training course or navigation subscription matches their instructor’s plan. Ask first. A gift should support training without creating a second system the student has to learn. If you cannot verify compatibility, choose a keepsake or a retailer gift card and let them select their own equipment.

The list

Our editorial order starts with gifts that support the student’s own training plan. Exact equipment choices belong with the student and instructor; these are recommendations, not hands-on test results.

  1. 1

    A contribution toward lessons

    Our first choice when the student is actively training: support the flying they already plan to do. Confirm how the school applies credit, what it covers, and whether it expires.

  2. 2

    The logbook their instructor recommends

    A useful starting gift only if they still need one. Get the requested format and avoid making the student transfer records just to use a decorative alternative.

    Official source: pilotmall.com ↗
  3. 3

    A practical pen and notebook

    Choose a reliable everyday pen and a notebook for study notes. Keep it separate from required records, and favor a format they already enjoy using.

    Official source: pilotmall.com ↗
  4. 4

    An exact requested flight bag

    Look at what they carry now and what needs organizing. A compact bag can make sense, but check dimensions and pockets instead of buying the largest student bundle.

    Official source: sportys.com ↗
  5. 5

    A suitable kneeboard

    Choose with the student after confirming their tablet, case, and preferences. A popular kneeboard is still a poor gift if it does not fit their actual setup.

    Official source: sportys.com ↗
  6. 6

    A headset fund

    Let the student and instructor identify suitable models and configurations. A clearly stated contribution avoids guessing about connectors, fit, or the student’s longer-term budget.

  7. 7

    Instructor-requested study materials

    Get the exact title, edition, or course link. Extra materials should support the existing syllabus instead of creating a competing study system.

  8. 8

    A light from their equipment list

    Use the instructor’s recommendation and confirm the exact item. Do not assume a novelty flashlight or a generic product listing establishes suitability for their training.

    Official source: sportys.com ↗
  9. 9

    A model of their training aircraft

    A personal keepsake can be the right choice when equipment needs are already covered. Confirm aircraft type, variant, and display space before choosing.

    Official source: pilotmall.com ↗
  10. 10

    A milestone photo and handwritten note

    Celebrate the person’s effort and the people supporting them. A specific memory and an accurate date can make a modest gift feel more meaningful than another gadget.

These are editorial recommendations and planning ideas, not hands-on test results. Read how we choose our picks.
